lead: One compile error hides every later one, so "the first red fixture line" moves backwards as you fix it.
body: A parse error suppresses name resolution entirely, so behind it can sit a member the spec says does not exist and a subscript that panics `nvs-ir`, none of them reported until the parse error is gone. Budget a fixture as "run it again after every fix until it exits 0", not as "one report, one slice" — and do not trust a handoff's claim about which line a fixture stops at without running it.
